$comment: Guided labs for your own subscription. Commands are Bash for Azure Cloud Shell. Each verify.expect is a list of regular expressions the pasted output must match; verify.sample is an example output the tests check against.

labs.title: Secure a storage account: TLS, no public access, data roles and lifecycle
labs.summary: Create a hardened storage account, upload a blob with your Entra identity instead of keys, and add a lifecycle rule that tiers and expires data.

cost.detail: A Standard_LRS account with a few KB of data costs fractions of a cent per day. Delete it when you finish.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (free account is fine)
Azure Cloud Shell (Bash) or Azure CLI 2.60+ signed in with az login
goals: Create a storage account with TLS 1.2 minimum and public blob access disabled
Use Storage Blob Data Contributor instead of account keys
Add a lifecycle management rule

steps.title: Set variables
steps.text: Pick names once. Storage account names must be globally unique, lower case, 3-24 characters.
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az104-storage
LOC=westeurope
SA=stlab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table

steps.title: Create the account
steps.text: Hardened from the start: HTTPS only (the default), TLS 1.2, no anonymous blob access.
steps.commands:
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG -l $LOC \
  --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2 \
  --min-tls-version TLS1_2 --allow-blob-public-access false

verify.command: az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query "{tls:minimumTlsVersion, publicBlob:allowBlobPublicAccess, https:enableHttpsTrafficOnly}" -o json
verify.explain: All three settings should come back exactly like this.

steps.title: Give yourself a data role
steps.text: Control-plane roles such as Owner do not let you read blob data with Entra ID. Assign a data role on the account. It can take a minute or two to apply.
steps.commands:
ME=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)
SAID=$(az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query id -o tsv)
az role assignment create --assignee $ME \
  --role "Storage Blob Data Contributor" --scope $SAID

steps.title: Upload a blob with your identity
steps.text: --auth-mode login uses your Entra token, so no account key is ever handled.
steps.commands:
az storage container create --account-name $SA -n docs --auth-mode login
echo "hello from the lab" > hello.txt
az storage blob upload --account-name $SA -c docs -n hello.txt -f hello.txt --auth-mode login

verify.command: az storage blob list --account-name $SA -c docs --auth-mode login --query "[].name" -o tsv
verify.explain: If you get AuthorizationPermissionMismatch, the role assignment has not propagated yet - wait a minute and retry.

steps.title: Add a lifecycle rule
steps.text: Move blobs to Cool after 30 days and delete them after 365.
steps.commands:
cat > policy.json <<'JSON'
{"rules":[{"enabled":true,"name":"tier-and-expire","type":"Lifecycle",
  "definition":{"filters":{"blobTypes":["blockBlob"],"prefixMatch":["docs/"]},
  "actions":{"baseBlob":{"tierToCool":{"daysAfterModificationGreaterThan":30},
  "delete":{"daysAfterModificationGreaterThan":365}}}}}]}
JSON
az storage account management-policy create --account-name $SA -g $RG --policy @policy.json

verify.command: az storage account management-policy show --account-name $SA -g $RG --query "policy.rules[0].name" -o tsv
verify.explain: The rule is saved; Azure runs lifecycle policies about once a day.

checklist: Account shows TLS1_2 and allowBlobPublicAccess false
Uploaded a blob with --auth-mode login (no keys)
Lifecycle rule tier-and-expire exists
I can explain why Owner alone could not read the blob

cleanup.commands:
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
rm -f hello.txt policy.json
cleanup.note: Deleting the resource group deletes the account and the role assignment scoped to it.

labs.title: VNet, subnets, an NSG and a private VM
labs.summary: Build a VNet with two subnets, lock SSH down to your own IP with a subnet NSG, and deploy a VM with no public IP that you manage through Run Command.

cost.detail: A Standard_B1s VM and its disk (750 B1s hours a month are included for 12 months on an eligible free account). Delete the group as soon as you finish - stopped VMs still pay for disks.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription
Cloud Shell (Bash) or Azure CLI
goals: Plan and create a VNet with subnets
Associate an NSG with a subnet and add a scoped rule
Deploy a VM without a public IP and inspect its effective rules

steps.title: Set variables
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az104-network
LOC=westeurope
MYIP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org)
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table

steps.title: Create the VNet and subnets
steps.text: A /16 for the VNet, a /24 per subnet - Azure keeps 5 addresses in each.
steps.commands:
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet-lab --address-prefixes 10.10.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name web --subnet-prefixes 10.10.1.0/24
az network vnet subnet create -g $RG --vnet-name vnet-lab -n data --address-prefixes 10.10.2.0/24

verify.command: az network vnet subnet list -g $RG --vnet-name vnet-lab --query "[].{name:name, prefix:addressPrefix}" -o table
verify.explain: Both subnets with their own ranges.

steps.title: Create the NSG and attach it to the web subnet
steps.text: Only your IP may reach port 22. Azure's default rules still deny all other inbound internet traffic.
steps.commands:
az network nsg create -g $RG -n nsg-web
az network nsg rule create -g $RG --nsg-name nsg-web -n allow-ssh-me --priority 100 \
  --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp \
  --source-address-prefixes $MYIP --destination-port-ranges 22
az network vnet subnet update -g $RG --vnet-name vnet-lab -n web --network-security-group nsg-web

steps.title: Deploy a VM with no public IP
steps.text: --public-ip-address "" and --nsg "" mean no public IP and no NIC-level NSG: the subnet NSG is the only filter.
steps.commands:
az vm create -g $RG -n vm-lab --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B1s \
  --vnet-name vnet-lab --subnet web --public-ip-address "" --nsg "" \
  --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys

steps.title: Run a command without SSH
steps.text: Run Command goes through the Azure agent - no inbound port needed.
steps.commands:
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm-lab --command-id RunShellScript \
  --scripts "hostname; ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

verify.sample:
Enable succeeded:
[stdout]
vm-lab
    inet 10.10.1.4/24 metric 100 brd 10.10.1.255 scope global eth0

[stderr]
verify.explain: The VM has a private address from the web subnet.

steps.title: Look at the effective rules
steps.text: What actually applies to the NIC: your rule plus Azure's defaults.
steps.commands:
az network nic list-effective-nsg -g $RG -n vm-labVMNic \
  --query "value[0].effectiveSecurityRules[].{name:name, access:access, priority:priority}" -o table

verify.sample:
Name                                   Access    Priority
-------------------------------------  --------  ----------
securityRules/allow-ssh-me             Allow     100
defaultSecurityRules/AllowVnetInBound  Allow     65000
defaultSecurityRules/AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound  Allow  65001
defaultSecurityRules/DenyAllInBound    Deny      65500
verify.explain: Your rule at 100, then the defaults ending in DenyAllInBound.

checklist: Two subnets with non-overlapping /24s
NSG associated with the web subnet, SSH only from my IP
VM has no public IP
Saw my rule and DenyAllInBound in the effective rules

cleanup.note: This deletes the VM, its disk and NIC, the NSG and the VNet. Check the portal afterwards: the group should be gone in a few minutes.

labs.title: Custom RBAC role with a scoped assignment
labs.summary: Write a least-privilege custom role that can only start, restart and read VMs, assign it at resource-group scope, and inspect what it grants.

cost.detail: Roles, assignments and empty resource groups cost nothing.

prerequisites: Owner or User Access Administrator on the subscription (needed to create custom roles)
Cloud Shell (Bash)
goals: Author a custom role definition
Assign it at the narrowest useful scope
Read back actions vs notActions

steps.title: Set variables
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az104-rbac
LOC=westeurope
SUB=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)
ME=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table

steps.title: Write the role
steps.text: Read everything in Compute, plus start and restart - nothing else.
steps.commands:
cat > role.json <<JSON
{
  "Name": "VM Operator (lab)",
  "Description": "Read, start and restart virtual machines.",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Compute/*/read",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action",
    "Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/read"
  ],
  "NotActions": [],
  "AssignableScopes": ["/subscriptions/$SUB"]
}
JSON
az role definition create --role-definition @role.json

verify.command: az role definition list --custom-role-only true --name "VM Operator (lab)" --query "[0].permissions[0].actions" -o tsv
verify.explain: New custom roles can take a few minutes to show up everywhere.

steps.title: Assign it at resource-group scope
steps.text: The narrowest scope that does the job.
steps.commands:
RGID=$(az group show -n $RG --query id -o tsv)
az role assignment create --assignee $ME --role "VM Operator (lab)" --scope $RGID

verify.explain: Assignments inherit down to everything in the group, and only there.

steps.title: Compare with built-in roles
steps.text: See why you did not use Virtual Machine Contributor.
steps.commands: az role definition list --name "Virtual Machine Contributor" --query "[0].permissions[0].actions" -o tsv | head -20

checklist: Custom role created with only the actions I need
Assigned at resource-group scope, not subscription
I can explain actions vs notActions vs dataActions
I can say why VM Contributor is broader (it includes listKeys on storage)

cleanup.commands:
az role assignment delete --assignee $ME --role "VM Operator (lab)" --scope $RGID
az role definition delete --name "VM Operator (lab)"
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
rm -f role.json
cleanup.note: Delete the assignment before the role definition - a role with assignments cannot be deleted.

labs.title: Azure Policy: allowed locations and a deny you can see
labs.summary: Assign the built-in Allowed locations policy at a resource group, watch a deployment fail with RequestDisallowedByPolicy, and check compliance.

cost.detail: Policy assignments and evaluation are free; the storage account you create in an allowed region costs a fraction of a cent.

prerequisites: Resource Policy Contributor or Owner on the subscription
Cloud Shell (Bash)
goals: Find a built-in policy definition
Assign it with parameters at resource-group scope
See Deny in action and read the compliance state

steps.title: Set variables
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az104-policy
LOC=westeurope
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table
RGID=$(az group show -n $RG --query id -o tsv)

steps.title: Find the built-in definition
steps.text: Look it up by display name rather than hard-coding a GUID.
steps.commands:
DEF=$(az policy definition list --query "[?displayName=='Allowed locations'].name | [0]" -o tsv)
echo $DEF

verify.explain: Built-in definitions are identified by a GUID name.

steps.title: Assign it to the resource group
steps.text: Only West Europe and North Europe allowed.
steps.commands:
az policy assignment create -n allowed-locations-lab --policy $DEF --scope $RGID \
  --params '{"listOfAllowedLocations":{"value":["westeurope","northeurope"]}}'

steps.title: Try a disallowed region
steps.text: Wait a few minutes after assigning, then create a storage account in East US. It must fail.
steps.commands: az storage account create -n stdeny$RANDOM -g $RG -l eastus --sku Standard_LRS

verify.sample: (RequestDisallowedByPolicy) Resource 'stdeny12345' was disallowed by policy. Policy identifiers: '[{"policyAssignment":{"name":"allowed-locations-lab"...
verify.explain: Being Owner does not bypass a Deny policy.

steps.title: Create one in an allowed region and check compliance
steps.text: Compliance scans run periodically; you can trigger one.
steps.commands:
az storage account create -n stok$RANDOM -g $RG -l westeurope --sku Standard_LRS -o none
az policy state trigger-scan -g $RG
az policy state summarize -g $RG --query "results.nonCompliantResources"

checklist: Found the definition by display name
Assignment scoped to the resource group with parameters
Saw RequestDisallowedByPolicy for eastus
Created a compliant resource in westeurope

cleanup.commands:
az policy assignment delete -n allowed-locations-lab --scope $RGID
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
cleanup.note: Delete the assignment first so it does not linger on an empty scope.

labs.title: Diagnostic settings to Log Analytics and a KQL query
labs.summary: Send a storage account's blob logs to a Log Analytics workspace, generate some traffic, and query it with KQL from the CLI.

cost.detail: Log Analytics bills per GB ingested; a lab produces a few KB. The workspace has no charge when empty. Delete it afterwards.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription
Cloud Shell (Bash)
goals: Create a Log Analytics workspace
Configure diagnostic settings on the blob service
Query StorageBlobLogs with KQL

steps.title: Set variables and resources
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az104-monitor
LOC=westeurope
SA=stmon$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table
az monitor log-analytics workspace create -g $RG -n law-lab -l $LOC -o none
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG -l $LOC --sku Standard_LRS -o none
LAWID=$(az monitor log-analytics workspace show -g $RG -n law-lab --query id -o tsv)
LAWGUID=$(az monitor log-analytics workspace show -g $RG -n law-lab --query customerId -o tsv)
SAID=$(az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query id -o tsv)

steps.title: Turn on diagnostic settings
steps.text: Blob logs are configured on the blob service, not the account.
steps.commands:
az monitor diagnostic-settings create -n to-law --resource "$SAID/blobServices/default" \
  --workspace $LAWID \
  --logs '[{"category":"StorageRead","enabled":true},{"category":"StorageWrite","enabled":true}]'

verify.explain: The setting exists on the blob service.

steps.title: Generate traffic
steps.text: A few writes and reads with the account key (fine for a throwaway lab).
steps.commands:
KEY=$(az storage account keys list -n $SA -g $RG --query "[0].value" -o tsv)
az storage container create --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY -n logs -o none
for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i > f$i.txt; az storage blob upload --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY -c logs -f f$i.txt -n f$i.txt -o none; done

steps.title: Query with KQL
steps.text: Logs take 5-15 minutes to arrive. If the result is empty, wait and run it again.
steps.commands:
az monitor log-analytics query -w $LAWGUID \
  --analytics-query "StorageBlobLogs | summarize count() by OperationName" -o table

verify.sample:
OperationName    Count_    TableName
---------------  --------  -------------
PutBlob          3         PrimaryResult
CreateContainer  1         PrimaryResult
verify.explain: Your uploads appear as PutBlob.

checklist: Workspace created
Diagnostic setting on blobServices/default
KQL query returns PutBlob rows
I know logs can take minutes to arrive

cleanup.commands:
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
rm -f f1.txt f2.txt f3.txt
cleanup.note: Deleting the group removes the workspace and the account. A deleted workspace can be recovered for 14 days unless you force-delete it.

labs.title: GitHub Actions deploys to App Service with OIDC (no secrets)
labs.summary: Create a free App Service, trust your GitHub repo's main branch with a federated credential, and deploy from a workflow without storing any password.

cost.detail: The F1 (Free) App Service plan costs nothing. Delete the group and the app registration when done.

prerequisites: A GitHub repository you own with a small Node app (or the sample below)
Permission to create app registrations in Entra ID
Cloud Shell (Bash)
goals: Create an app registration with a federated credential for one branch
Grant it the least role needed
Deploy with azure/login using OIDC

steps.title: Set variables
steps.text: Replace OWNER/REPO with your repository.
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az400-oidc
LOC=westeurope
APP=web-oidc-$RANDOM
REPO=OWNER/REPO
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table

steps.title: Create the web app
steps.text: A Linux F1 plan and a Node web app.
steps.commands:
az appservice plan create -g $RG -n plan-lab --sku F1 --is-linux
az webapp create -g $RG -p plan-lab -n $APP --runtime "NODE:20-lts"

verify.explain: The app exists and is running.

steps.title: Create the identity and trust GitHub
steps.text: The federated credential trusts tokens for the main branch of this repo only.
steps.commands:
CLIENT_ID=$(az ad app create --display-name gh-oidc-lab --query appId -o tsv)
az ad sp create --id $CLIENT_ID -o none
cat > fic.json <<JSON
{"name":"gh-main","issuer":"https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
 "subject":"repo:$REPO:ref:refs/heads/main","audiences":["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]}
JSON
az ad app federated-credential create --id $CLIENT_ID --parameters fic.json
RGID=$(az group show -n $RG --query id -o tsv)
az role assignment create --assignee $CLIENT_ID --role "Website Contributor" --scope $RGID
echo "AZURE_CLIENT_ID=$CLIENT_ID"; echo "AZURE_TENANT_ID=$(az account show --query tenantId -o tsv)"; echo "AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)"

verify.command: az ad app federated-credential list --id $CLIENT_ID --query "[0].subject" -o tsv
verify.explain: The subject must match the branch exactly - a push from another branch will be refused.

steps.title: Add the workflow
steps.text: Save the three IDs as repository secrets or variables (they are identifiers, not passwords), then commit this as .github/workflows/deploy.yml and push to main.
steps.commands:
cat <<'YAML'
name: deploy
on: { push: { branches: [main] } }
permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: YOUR_APP_NAME
          package: .
YAML

steps.title: Check the deployment
steps.text: After the push, check the run (or open the repository's Actions tab), then browse to the site.
steps.commands:
gh run list --repo $REPO --workflow deploy.yml --limit 1 --json conclusion -q '.[0].conclusion'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://$APP.azurewebsites.net

verify.explain: The workflow logged in with OIDC and deployed. A failure at azure/login usually means the federated credential subject does not match the branch.

checklist: No client secret was created anywhere
Federated credential subject pins repo and branch
Role is Website Contributor on the resource group, not Contributor on the subscription
Workflow has permissions: id-token: write

cleanup.commands:
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
az ad app delete --id $CLIENT_ID
rm -f fic.json
cleanup.note: Delete the app registration too - it lives in Entra ID, outside the resource group.

labs.title: Azure Pipelines: multi-stage YAML with an approval
labs.summary: Create an Azure DevOps project from the CLI, add a build-and-deploy YAML pipeline with an environment that needs approval, and run it.

cost.detail: Azure DevOps is free for up to 5 users. New organisations may need to request the free Microsoft-hosted parallel job (or use a self-hosted agent).

prerequisites: An Azure DevOps organisation (dev.azure.com)
Azure CLI with the azure-devops extension (az extension add -n azure-devops)
git
goals: Script project and pipeline creation
Use stages, a deployment job and an environment
Gate production with an approval

steps.title: Set defaults
steps.text: Replace ORG with your organisation name.
steps.commands:
ORG=https://dev.azure.com/ORG
az devops configure --defaults organization=$ORG
az devops project create --name az400-lab -o table
az devops configure --defaults organization=$ORG project=az400-lab

steps.title: Push a pipeline file
steps.text: The project's default repository has the project's name.
steps.commands:
git clone $(az repos show -r az400-lab --query remoteUrl -o tsv) lab && cd lab
cat > azure-pipelines.yml <<'YAML'
trigger: [main]
pool: { vmImage: ubuntu-latest }
stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: build
        steps:
          - script: echo "building $(Build.BuildNumber)" > out.txt
          - publish: out.txt
            artifact: drop
  - stage: Prod
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - deployment: deploy
        environment: prod
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - script: cat $(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/out.txt
YAML
git add . && git commit -m "Add pipeline" && git push -u origin HEAD:main

steps.title: Create the pipeline
steps.commands:
az pipelines create --name lab-ci --repository az400-lab --repository-type tfsgit \
  --branch main --yml-path azure-pipelines.yml --skip-first-run true -o table

steps.title: Add the approval
steps.text: In the portal: Pipelines → Environments → prod → ⋯ → Approvals and checks → Approvals → add yourself. (Approvals are not available from the CLI.) Then run the pipeline and approve it when it pauses before Prod.
steps.commands: az pipelines run --name lab-ci -o table

verify.command: az pipelines runs list --pipeline-ids $(az pipelines show --name lab-ci --query id -o tsv) --top 1 --query "[0].result" -o tsv
verify.explain: After you approve, the run finishes.

checklist: Two stages with dependsOn
Prod uses a deployment job and the prod environment
The run waited for my approval
I can say why approvals live on environments, not in YAML

cleanup.commands:
cd .. && rm -rf lab
az devops project delete --id $(az devops project show -p az400-lab --query id -o tsv) --yes
cleanup.note: Deleting the project removes the repo, pipeline and environment. It stays recoverable for 28 days.

labs.title: Azure Artifacts: publish and consume a versioned package
labs.summary: Create a feed, publish a Universal Package with a semantic version from the CLI, then download it by version - the basis of promoting build outputs.

cost.detail: Azure Artifacts includes 2 GiB of storage free per organisation.

prerequisites: The az400-lab project from the pipelines lab (or any project)
Azure CLI with the azure-devops extension
goals: Create a project-scoped feed
Publish a package version
Consume a specific version

steps.title: Create the feed
steps.text: In the portal: Artifacts → Create Feed → name lab-feed, scope Project (feeds can't be created from the az devops CLI). Then set variables.
steps.commands:
ORG=https://dev.azure.com/ORG
PROJECT=az400-lab

steps.title: Publish version 1.0.0
steps.text: Universal Packages hold any files - here a tiny 'tool'.
steps.commands:
mkdir -p tool && echo 'echo hello from 1.0.0' > tool/run.sh
az artifacts universal publish --organization $ORG --project $PROJECT --scope project \
  --feed lab-feed --name lab-tool --version 1.0.0 --description "Lab tool" --path ./tool

steps.title: Publish 1.1.0
steps.text: Versions are immutable: you cannot overwrite 1.0.0, so a change is a new version.
steps.commands:
echo 'echo hello from 1.1.0' > tool/run.sh
az artifacts universal publish --organization $ORG --project $PROJECT --scope project \
  --feed lab-feed --name lab-tool --version 1.1.0 --path ./tool

steps.title: Consume a pinned version
steps.commands:
az artifacts universal download --organization $ORG --project $PROJECT --scope project \
  --feed lab-feed --name lab-tool --version 1.0.0 --path ./download
cat download/run.sh

verify.explain: You got exactly the version you asked for.

checklist: Feed created with project scope
Published 1.0.0 and 1.1.0
Downloaded 1.0.0 by version
I can explain feed views (@local, @prerelease, @release) for promotion

cleanup.note: Delete the feed in the portal (Artifacts → feed settings → Delete feed), or delete the whole project.

labs.title: Pipeline secrets from Key Vault, never in YAML
labs.summary: Store a secret in an RBAC-mode Key Vault and read it in a GitHub Actions workflow through OIDC, masked in the logs.

cost.detail: Key Vault charges per 10,000 operations; a lab uses a handful.

prerequisites: The OIDC app registration from the GitHub Actions lab (CLIENT_ID), or create one the same way
Cloud Shell (Bash)
goals: Create a Key Vault using the Azure RBAC permission model
Grant the pipeline identity Key Vault Secrets User only
Read and mask the secret in a workflow

steps.title: Set variables and create the vault
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az400-kv
LOC=westeurope
KV=kv-lab-$RANDOM
ME=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table
az keyvault create -n $KV -g $RG -l $LOC --enable-rbac-authorization true -o none
KVID=$(az keyvault show -n $KV --query id -o tsv)

steps.title: Add a secret
steps.text: You need a data-plane role to write secrets, even as Owner.
steps.commands:
az role assignment create --assignee $ME --role "Key Vault Secrets Officer" --scope $KVID -o none
sleep 30
az keyvault secret set --vault-name $KV -n db-password --value "$(openssl rand -base64 18)" -o none

verify.explain: If you see Forbidden, wait a minute for the role assignment and retry.

steps.title: Let the pipeline read it
steps.text: Read-only, on this vault only.
steps.commands: az role assignment create --assignee $CLIENT_ID --role "Key Vault Secrets User" --scope $KVID

verify.sample:
Key Vault Secrets Officer
Key Vault Secrets User
verify.explain: You can write; the pipeline can only read.

steps.title: Read it in the workflow
steps.text: Add these steps after azure/login in your workflow. add-mask hides the value from the logs.
steps.commands:
cat <<'YAML'
      - name: Get secret
        run: |
          value=$(az keyvault secret show --vault-name YOUR_KV -n db-password --query value -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$value"
          echo "DB_PASSWORD=$value" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: echo "The password is $DB_PASSWORD"   # prints ***
YAML

checklist: Vault uses the Azure RBAC permission model
Pipeline identity has Key Vault Secrets User only
The secret appears as *** in the run log
No secret value is stored in the repository

cleanup.commands:
az group delete -n $RG --yes
az keyvault purge -n $KV
cleanup.note: Key Vault soft delete keeps the name reserved for 90 days; purging frees it (purge protection is off in this lab).

labs.title: Build in ACR and run on Container Apps
labs.summary: Build an image in Azure Container Registry without Docker on your machine, then run it on Azure Container Apps pulling with a managed identity.

cost.detail: ACR Basic is about $0.17 per day; Container Apps' consumption plan has a monthly free grant. Delete everything the same day.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription
Cloud Shell (Bash) - the containerapp extension installs on first use
goals: Use az acr build (no local Docker)
Pull with a managed identity instead of admin credentials
Expose the app with external ingress

steps.title: Set variables and create the registry
steps.commands:
RG=rg-az400-aca
LOC=westeurope
ACR=acrlab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC -o table
az acr create -n $ACR -g $RG --sku Basic -o none

steps.title: Build the image in ACR
steps.text: ACR Tasks builds in Azure from your local folder.
steps.commands:
mkdir -p app && cd app echo '

Hello from Container Apps

' > index.html printf 'FROM nginx:alpine\nCOPY index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html\n' > Dockerfile az acr build -r $ACR -t hello:v1 . cd ..

verify.command: az acr repository show-tags -n $ACR --repository hello -o tsv
verify.explain: The image is in your registry.

steps.title: Create the environment and the app
steps.text: --registry-identity system gives the app a managed identity with AcrPull - no admin user or password.
steps.commands:
az containerapp env create -n cae-lab -g $RG -l $LOC -o none
az containerapp create -n ca-lab -g $RG --environment cae-lab \
  --image $ACR.azurecr.io/hello:v1 --registry-server $ACR.azurecr.io --registry-identity system \
  --ingress external --target-port 80 -o none

steps.title: Browse to it
steps.commands:
FQDN=$(az containerapp show -n ca-lab -g $RG --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv)
curl -s https://$FQDN

verify.explain: Served over HTTPS by Container Apps.

checklist: Built with az acr build
Registry admin user stays disabled
App pulls with a system-assigned managed identity
Reached the app over HTTPS

cleanup.note: This removes the registry (and its daily charge), the environment and the app.
